title: Metadata ledger for key-sync and evidence handoff
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a compact, auditable metadata ledger that captures state changes for tenant encryption keys (wrap/unwrap events, HSM key identifiers, rotation markers, and residency-affinity tags) and produces deterministic evidence bundles for compliance reporting. The ledger is not a replacement for primary audit logs; it is a tamper-evident summary optimized for regulatory evidence exports and cross-region reconciliation.

Scope:
- Define a minimal canonical schema for ledger entries (event_type, time, tenant_id, key_id_hash, hsm_event_ref, rotation_epoch, region_affinity, proof_digest).
- Implement a producer shim in KMS adapter that emits ledger entries on key lifecycle events (create, rotate, disable, rewrap).
- Store ledger shards as append-only objects in the immutable S3 bucket (object-versioning + retention), with a parallel write to a signed Kafka topic for near realtime monitoring.
- Build an "evidence handoff" worker that consumes ledger shards, assembles a deterministic evidence bundle (ledger shard + accompanying HSM-signed event refs + compact index), signs the bundle with the platform signing key, and uploads to the compliance store for export.

Design constraints / tradeoffs considered:
- Minimal vs verbose entries: chose minimal canonical schema to reduce sensitivity exposure while keeping enough context to reconstruct proofs during audits.
- Immutability location: using S3 with retention/lock for long-term storage (pros: simple, durable; cons: eventual amplification of storage costs).
- HSM references: we will not store raw HSM material; only signed event references (HSM UUID + event_digest) to preserve security boundaries.
- Performance: ledger writes must be non-blocking for KMS paths; will use background batching and acknowledge KMS path before evidence bundling completes.

Out of scope: full-text audit logs export, per-token encryption telemetry, or user-facing UI for browsing ledger entries (handled later in console-2026.08).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical ledger entry schema is documented in Confluence and reviewed by Security
KMS adapter emits ledger entries on key create/rotate/disable events without increasing KMS latency by >5ms p50
Ledger shards are written as append-only objects to the compliance S3 bucket with object lock enabled
Evidence handoff worker produces a signed bundle and exposes an immutable object URL in the compliance store
Automated smoke tests validate that a sample rotation event produces a verifiable evidence bundle (cryptographic signature verifies)
comments: 2026-02-17 - Lena Chen: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence; security asked for explicit schema field describing 'key_id_hash' instead of plaintext key ids.

2026-02-25 - Oliver Brooks: Prototype shim in kms-adapter implemented and smoke-tested against local HSM emulator. Observed ~2ms additional p50 on key create; acceptable. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kms-adapter/pulls/348

2026-03-02 - Security (Aisha Patel): Requested threat model and confirmation that no secret key material is stored; also asked for rotation_epoch semantics to be clarified. Updated schema to include rotation_epoch and event_nonce.

2026-03-07 - QA (Miguel Santos): End-to-end test added to compliance-bundler PR; failing intermittently due to eventual consistency in S3 object listing — mitigation: use deterministic object keys including shard-seq + checksum.
2026-03-10 - Oliver Brooks: Switched evidence handoff worker to sign bundles with platform signing key (KMS-backed) and added verification script to CI. Marking integration tests stable on staging.
